**Theme:** GPT-5.6 lands in the Polymarket hot zone; 53 power plants target June kickoff as FERC's 60-day RTO clock ticks; moratorium wave crosses state lines into Nevada and Iowa.

## Data Science & Analytics
- GPT-5.6 expected within days; Polymarket 83% odds for June 22–28 window ($960K wagered). Rumored: 1.5M token context, sharper long-horizon coding. Sub-60-day release cadence continues.
- Google I/O shipped Gemini 3.5 Flash as default model globally. Outperforms 3.1 Pro on coding/agentic benchmarks at 4× speed, ~40% lower cost ($1.50/M input). Information agents announced for summer.
- Anthropic S-1 under SEC review; $47B revenue (12-month run); $965B private valuation after $65B Series H. First major AI lab to formally begin IPO process. Fable/Mythos export ban persists.
- AlphaSignal: agentic harness engineering emerging as competitive axis. Self-Harness raised Terminal-Bench 2.0 from 40.5% to 61.9% with base weights fixed. 10-layer scaffolding technique.
- NVIDIA-SK hynix multiyear memory co-development deal for Vera Rubin, RTX Spark, Jetson Thor. NAVER commits to gigawatt-scale DSX AI factories (55 MW start, Sejong).

## Energy Buildout & Infrastructure
- Industrial Info Resources: 53 utility-scale power plants target June kickoff — $19.2B, 12 GW (56% gas, 26% solar, 17% wind). Heaviest in ERCOT and MISO.
- BNEF raises U.S. DC power demand forecast 36% to 106 GW by 2035 (from 25 GW in 2024). PJM alone could add 31 GW DC load in 5 years. Grid Strategies counters: closer to 65 GW by 2030.
- Elementl Power announces 1.5 GW SMR project in SE Ohio (Meigs County). Five GE Vernova BWRX-300 reactors. PJM interconnection filed for 600 MW. Construction 2030, first unit 2034.
- FERC 60-day RTO tariff clock ticking — responses due mid-August. PJM EIT operational; other RTOs have not disclosed approach.

## Rural Development Opportunities
- Woodbury County IA votes on 1-year DC moratorium June 23. All five supervisors support. MidAmerican Energy DC on 900 acres Salix. Jurisdiction gap: DC in city limits, moratorium covers unincorporated.
- Reno NV extends DC moratorium through August 2027 (6-1 vote, June 1). Cannot lift until regs adopted across ~12 topic areas. Waiting for NV 2027 legislative session.
- Hochul signals no rush on NY moratorium; has until December. Sympathetic to bill concerns but favors municipal-level decisions. Re-election in November.
- USDA broadband grant deadlines this week: Community Connect $17M (June 29), DLT $27M (June 30). REAP frozen. REDLG also June 30.
- Larimer County CO moratorium through Aug 25; drafting DC land use code. No applications submitted. Front Range moratoriums: Denver, Larimer, others discussing.

## Cross-Sector Signals
- Moratorium geography expanding west (Reno NV, Larimer CO). 14 states now considered or enacted DC moratoriums. Woodbury County vote tomorrow tests Iowa formalization.
- SMR pipeline broadening beyond existing nuclear sites. Elementl Power Ohio = greenfield build. Four distinct SMR deployment models now in play.
- Inference efficiency gains (Gemini 3.5 Flash 40% cheaper, harness engineering +50% gains) may moderate but not reverse DC power demand. BNEF 106 GW assumes current efficiency trends.

**Theme:** OpenAI's IPO strategy fractures from Anthropic's on RSI grounds; half the global DC pipeline faces equipment-driven delay; Iowa moratorium vote tomorrow tests county jurisdiction limits.

## Data Science & Analytics
- GPT-5.6 launch window opens June 22. Polymarket odds shifted: "Not released by June 28" leads at 58% ($1.1M wagered). 1.5M context, alignment pipeline redesign, reasoning budget 768→960. No official release as of PM June 22.
- OpenAI delays IPO — Altman cites RSI risk. Confidential S-1 filed May 22, targeting September listing. Public S-1 expected late July. Anthropic filed June 1, targets October Nasdaq.
- Perplexity "Search as Code" architecture (June 1 paper): agents write Python to call search stacks directly instead of looping tool calls. 85% token reduction on 200-CVE task per AlphaSignal.

## AI in Practice
- Colorado AI Act gutted by SB 189 (signed May 14). Effective date pushed to Jan 1, 2027. Original framework (risk management, impact assessments, AG reporting) replaced with transparency-only disclosure obligations + 3-year record-keeping + 60-day cure period.
- Deloitte 2026 State of AI: 72% of enterprises have production AI workloads. 40% of apps to embed agents by year-end. 60% governance gap. Companies WITH governance frameworks push 12× more projects to production.
- EU AI Act: August 2 transparency + high-risk rules, but Digital Omnibus (May) provisionally extends deadlines.

## Energy Buildout & Infrastructure
- Sightline Climate: 30-50% of 16 GW 2026 DC pipeline will not materialize on schedule. Only 5 GW under construction. Bottleneck: transformers, switchgear, batteries. 26% slipped in 2025.
- IREN expands to three continents: 800 MW Australia campus (June 3), Nostrum Group Europe acquisition (June 15). Extends NVIDIA $5.5B partnership.
- Oklo SMR pipeline: 14 GW total — 1.2 GW Ohio + 12 GW Switch + 500 MW Equinix. $10B+ backing. None delivers before 2030.
- Goldman Sachs: DC demand 31 GW (2025) → 41 GW (2026) → 66 GW (2027).

## Rural Development Opportunities
- Woodbury County IA votes June 23 on 1-year moratorium. All 5 supervisors support. Jurisdiction gap: DC in Salix city limits, moratorium covers unincorporated only.
- USDA grant deadlines: Community Connect $17M (June 29), DLT $27M (June 30). REAP frozen. REDLG June 30.

## Cross-Sector Signals
- Equipment bottlenecks bridge energy and compute: Sightline slippage implies demand forecasts overstate near-term buildout.
- Governance as competitive moat: Colorado/EU rollbacks leave governance voluntary; Deloitte 12× multiplier makes it a deployment accelerator.
- Rural jurisdiction gaps widening: county moratoriums cannot reach city-annexed projects; state legislatures hold the lever.

**Theme:** FERC fires its biggest shot at grid bottlenecks; Iowa joins the moratorium wave; GM bets sodium-ion can power the data center buildout.

## Data Science & Analytics
- GPT-5.6 expected within days; Polymarket 83% odds for June 22–28 window. Chief scientist calls it "a meaningful leap" in agentic workflows. Sub-60-day release cadence (5.4 March, 5.5 April 23).
- HPE and NVIDIA expand AI Factory at Discover Las Vegas (June 15–18): added Vera CPU, Agent Toolkit, Confidential Computing. NemoClaw observability Q4 2026.
- Oracle cut 30,000 jobs (18% headcount) March 31 to fund $50B AI DC buildout. $8–10B annual cash freed. Cerner/OCI/ERP consulting hit hardest; AI/security protected.
- Alteryx unveils Agent Studio and MCP Server at Inspire 2026 — analysts can convert workflows to autonomous agents. MCP protocol adoption widens beyond dev tools.

## Energy Buildout & Infrastructure
- FERC issued landmark Section 206 show-cause orders (June 18) to all six RTOs/ISOs: justify or rewrite large-load interconnection tariffs within 60 days. 30-day reliability report required. Covers 200M Americans, 30+ states. Most aggressive federal grid-connection action yet.
- FERC approved PJM expedited interconnection track (June 9): 10 projects/year, 250 MW min, 3-year commercial deadline. $500K study deposit + $15K/MW readiness deposit. 100% network upgrade costs on applicant. Expires end 2027.
- SC PSC approved Dominion-Santee Cooper $5B, 2,180 MW Canadys gas plant (June 12). Colleton County. Environmental groups flagged Edisto River siting.
- GM-Peak Energy partnership (June 9): GM manufactures sodium-ion cells in Michigan; Peak integrates into passively cooled storage (20% cost cut vs lithium-ion, 99%+ uptime). Trial production 2028. Targets utilities and DCs.
- Behind-the-meter DC gas plants escape state rate regulation, may raise bills more than grid connection. PJM proposed 50 MW BTM netting threshold (Feb). White House Ratepayer Protection Pledge (March) is nonbinding.

## Rural Development Opportunities
- Woodbury County IA: all five supervisors support one-year DC moratorium (June 17). MidAmerican Energy confirmed DC under consideration on 900 acres Salix annexed April. Vote expected June 23. Iowa is 10th state with active moratorium efforts.
- NY data center moratorium awaits Hochul. Passed June 5 (Senate 44-16, Assembly 102-39). Industry lobbying for veto. Hochul has expressed reservations. 10-day clock starts on delivery.
- USDA broadband grants: Community Connect ($17M, deadline June 29) and DLT ($27M, deadline June 30). REAP grants frozen. REDLG deadline June 30.
- Champlain Hudson Power Express: 1,250 MW HVDC from Quebec to NYC hit commercial operation May 13 (early). 10.4 TWh/yr, $97.50/MWh (yr 1), 25-year contract. 339 miles, longest buried line in North America. 20% of NYC power.

## Cross-Sector Signals
- FERC Section 206 orders force all RTOs to confront large-load interconnection simultaneously. If costs shift to DCs, rural self-generation sites gain advantage — but behind-the-meter gas loophole compounds ratepayer problem.
- Moratorium movement: Iowa = 10th state. Jurisdiction contests continue (Woodbury mirrors Hood County TX pattern). Hochul decision will set national precedent.
- Sodium-ion storage (GM-Peak Energy) converges with gas plant cost spiral. If 20% cost reduction materializes at scale by 2028–29, offers domestic non-lithium alternative as gas turbine slots sold out into next decade.

**Theme:** SpaceX sets IPO record at $75B; New York legislature passes first-in-nation data center moratorium; GE Vernova gas turbine backlog hits 100 GW; FERC large-load rule due any day.

## Data Science & Analytics
- SpaceX priced IPO at $135/share on June 11, raised ~$75B (largest U.S. IPO ever). Shares opened June 12 on Nasdaq under SPCX, closed +19%. Anthropic S-1 under SEC review; OpenAI filing expected next.
- Google TurboQuant (ICLR 2026) compresses KV cache to 3 bits with zero accuracy loss — 6× memory reduction, 8× faster on H100. No retraining required. Open-source adoption accelerating.
- Google Gemini 3.5 Pro nears June GA with 2M-token context and Deep Think reasoning. Absorbs former Ultra tier. Limited enterprise preview ongoing; no firm date.
- OpenAI launched Deployment Company (DeployCo) May 11 with $4B+ backing from TPG, Advent, Bain Capital, Brookfield. Acquired Scottish consultancy Tomoro (150 engineers). Clients include Tesco, Virgin Atlantic.

## Energy Buildout & Infrastructure
- GE Vernova gas turbine backlog hit 100 GW in Q1 2026 (targeting 110 GW by year-end). Q1 orders +71% YoY to $18.3B. Siemens Energy: €136B record backlog + $1B U.S. mfg investment. Slots sold into next decade at all three OEMs.
- FERC large-load interconnection rule (RM26-4-000) due by end of June. Key debates: 20 MW threshold, 60-day expedited studies, cost allocation. SPP HILL initiative approved Jan as interim model.
- PJM capacity costs: $329/MW-day for 2026/27. Data centers drove 45% of $47.2B across three auctions. 2027/28 forecast adds 5,250 MW peak load (5,100 MW = data centers). Ratepayers face +$1.4B in capacity costs starting June 2026.
- NextEra-Dominion $66.8B merger proceeding through SEC 425 filings. Combined entity: ~10M customers across FL/VA/NC/SC. Expected close H2 2027.

## Rural Development Opportunities
- New York legislature passed Responsible Data Center Development Act (A11560/S10642) — first state-level moratorium bill. Senate 44-16, Assembly 102-39. One-year pause on permits ≥20 MW. Awaits Governor Hochul.
- Hill County TX rescinded moratorium June 5 after $100M lawsuit from RCM Hill LLC. Hood County also sued. Somervell County passed symbolic resolution opposing DCs until state acts. Nearly half of planned TX DCs target unincorporated areas.
- Superior WI passed unanimous one-year moratorium June 16. Shawano County WI board vote June 24. Denver enacted unanimous one-year moratorium May 19 (blocking CoreSite campus expansion).
- Pulaski County AR revised moratorium in committee after vote miscount. Targets facilities ≥5 MW or ≥100K gallons/day.

## Cross-Sector Signals
- Data center moratorium movement has gone national: NY state legislature, Denver major metro, Superior WI, Pulaski County AR all new since June 4. Hill County TX rescission shows developer counter-force via litigation.
- Gas turbine bottleneck meets nuclear ambition: GE Vernova 100 GW backlog and decade-long queues explain why operators keep signing SMR deals. But SMRs are 2028+ at earliest.
- SpaceX IPO opens floodgate for AI-adjacent public offerings: Anthropic and OpenAI have live pricing benchmark. Combined 2026 listings could pull $200B+ from public markets.

- BNEF: Gas plant construction costs +66% since 2023 ($2,157/kW). Turbine prices 195% above 2019 levels. Build timelines +23%.
- 53 utility-scale projects ($19.2B) targeting June construction start across North America. Gas leads at 6.8 GW (56%), solar 3.1 GW (26%), wind 2.1 GW (17%).
- Google-Voltus 100 MW VPP in PJM — first hyperscaler-VPP deal in U.S. wholesale market. Google has 1 GW demand response across Entergy Arkansas, Minnesota Power, DTE.

- USDA accepting applications for $44M in rural broadband grants. Community Connect ($17M, deadline June 29) and DLT ($27M, deadline June 30).

- Data center moratorium movement now coast-to-coast: Imperial County CA, Boone County IN, NY state, Denver, Superior WI. Abbott TX directive + Warner/Van Hollen federal bill = competing regulatory models.
- Gas plant cost spiral feeds nuclear/VPP alternatives. Google-Voltus VPP and NuScale/TVA SMR pipeline look less like hedges, more like necessities.
- Anthropic export-control crisis may reshape AI infrastructure geography — domestic-only DC deployment model could boost rural siting for compliance-driven builds.

**Theme:** AI firms race toward trillion-dollar IPOs; DOE builds grid simulation for data center power shocks; moratorium movement spreads to Wisconsin and Fort Worth.

## Data Science & Analytics
- Anthropic files confidentially for IPO at $965B valuation after $65B Series H; annualized revenue run rate to top $50B by July. OpenAI ($852B) preparing own filing. SpaceX roadshow begins June 4, targeting $1.75T listing June 12.
- DOE launches Agora test bed at National Laboratory of the Rockies — first national-lab facility dedicated to simulating hyperscale data center power behavior on the grid. Funded by Office of Electricity and industry partners.
- M Science (Jefferies subsidiary) launches Unified Data Model + MCP Server for institutional investors. Signals MCP protocol adoption spreading beyond developer tooling into finance.
- EIA projects record 86 GW of new U.S. generating capacity in 2026: solar 43.4 GW (51%), battery storage 24 GW (28%), wind 11.8 GW (14%), natural gas 6.3 GW. Texas = 40% of solar, 53% of battery storage.

## Energy Buildout & Infrastructure
- FERC set to act on large-load interconnection rule (RM26-4-000) by end of June. Key questions: 60-day expedited studies for flexible loads; full cost allocation for grid upgrades. Still at ANOPR stage.
- Sens. Warner and Van Hollen introduce bipartisan Power for the People Act: requires DCs to bring own generation + storage, accept curtailment. Cites $21B in PJM capacity costs, $840/yr household bill increase by 2028. Virginia prices +14.5% in past year.
- Louisiana PSC fast-tracks (4-1) Entergy's 7,400 MW gas build-out for Meta's $27B Holly Ridge data center. Seven new plants beyond three approved. Also plans 2,500 MW solar + batteries. Final vote Nov–Dec. 4,000 temp workers swelled Richland Parish population 20%.
- NextEra-Dominion $66.8B merger: SEC 425 filings underway. Requires FERC, NRC, HSR, plus VA/NC/SC state approvals. Expected close H2 2027.

## Rural Development Opportunities
- McMinnville TN passes 18-month data center moratorium after 25 MW / 96,000 sq ft NVIDIA GB200 NVL72 facility proposed. Requires water, energy, environmental, sound impact studies. ~3,000-signature petition.
- Shawano County WI planning committee recommends 1-year moratorium on DC permits in unincorporated areas — first Wisconsin action. Unanimous public hearing support. Full board vote June 24.
- Fort Worth TX residents demand moratorium but state law blocks municipal pause on planned DCs. Council will vote August on DC regulations (water, noise, land use). Separate crypto mining ban proposed. DCs contributed $83M in property taxes over 5 years.
- USDA RBDG and REDLG applications close June 30. REAP grants frozen (EO 14315). RUS Section 313A bond guarantee NOFO open May 22–July 6. RUS has invested $10.4B in rural electric infrastructure since Jan 2025.

## Cross-Sector Signals
- Moratorium movement now spans 4 states (TX, TN, WI, VA). Fort Worth blocked by state law shows patchwork — federal legislation (Power for the People Act) now also in play.
- FERC interconnection rule (supply-side) and Power for the People Act (demand-side cost allocation) converging. Both moving in June. Together would reshape how DCs connect and pay.
- Entergy-Meta Louisiana = rural development story in miniature: $27B investment, 7,400 MW gas, 20% population surge, road/housing strain — alongside $2B projected property taxes and 6,500 construction jobs.

- NVIDIA equity investments top $40B across AI stack: $3.2B Corning (optical fiber, NC/TX), $2.1B IREN, $2B Coherent.
- OpenAI GPT-5.6 targeting June release; Anthropic Mythos also expected June. OpenAI IPO prep at ~$1T valuation, $20B+ annualized revenue.
- Penn Engineering Mollifier Layers for scientific AI (inverse PDEs), to appear at NeurIPS 2026.
- Harvard/Beth Israel study in Science: OpenAI reasoning model outperformed physicians on ED diagnoses using EHR data.

## Energy Buildout & Infrastructure
- PJM capacity auction: record $16.4B, $333.44/MW-day clearing price (3rd consecutive record). Data centers = 40% ($6.5B). 32 GW demand growth through 2030, nearly all from DCs. Residential bills up 1.5-5% starting June 2026.

- Gas turbine bottleneck: GE Vernova targeting 110 GW backlog by year-end, scaling to 80 units/year. Siemens $1B U.S. expansion, GE Vernova $600M. Wait times up to 7 years.
- EIA: 86 GW new generating capacity planned for 2026 (record). Solar 51%, battery 28%, wind 14%. But 1,350+ GW stuck in interconnection queues.
- NuScale/ENTRA1/TVA: 6 GW SMR program (~72 modules), first power ~2030. Oklo pipeline 14 GW (Switch, Equinix, Meta), NRC design criteria approved May 2026.

- Meta $27B Richland Parish LA: 4M sq ft, $2B+ property taxes, $200M local infra, 6,500 construction jobs. Also $10B+ Lebanon IN campus (1 GW, 1,500 acres).
- Applied Digital: ABB partnership expanded for 300 MW Polaris Forge 2 (Harwood ND). Minnkota $110M 345-kV substation targeting Sept completion. Oliver County 430 MW still under evaluation.
- Vantage Data Centers: $25B, 1.4 GW "Frontier" campus in Shackelford County TX (pop ~3,500). 5,000+ construction jobs.
- Maine governor vetoed first-in-nation state data center moratorium (20 MW+ threshold).

## Cross-Sector Signals
- Hill County lawsuit will test rural county authority over data center siting; if developer wins, fight shifts to state legislatures.
- PJM 40% DC cost share + FERC interconnection rule = cost allocation decision will shape rural community attitudes toward data centers.

*Export controls, coast-to-coast moratoriums, and gas cost inflation reshaped the data center buildout calculus in a single week.*

**Note:** This digest draws from Tuesday's AM and PM briefings (June 17) — the only editions filed this week — plus the running trend tracker. Coverage gaps on Monday, Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday mean some stories may have developed without capture.

---

## Top Movers

**1. Anthropic Fable/Mythos Export Ban Lands**
Commerce Department classified Anthropic's Fable 5 and Mythos 5 as export-controlled on June 12; Anthropic disabled both models globally. Cybersecurity professionals issued an open letter protesting the decision, and a federal judge had already blocked an earlier Pentagon-originated ban in March. This is the first time a frontier AI model has been pulled from global availability by U.S. trade controls. If sustained, it forces a nationality-based access bifurcation and could push Anthropic toward domestic-only data center deployments — a direct tailwind for rural U.S. siting.
**Watch next week:** Whether Commerce narrows the scope or Anthropic seeks injunctive relief.

**2. Data Center Moratorium Movement Goes Coast-to-Coast**
Imperial County CA (first California county, June 16), Boone County IN (12th Indiana county, June 15), and Superior WI (June 16) all passed moratoriums this week. New York's legislature sent the first state-level moratorium bill to Governor Hochul (Senate 44-16, Assembly 102-39). Denver's one-year pause blocks CoreSite expansion. Meanwhile, Hill County TX rescinded its moratorium after a $100M developer lawsuit — showing the counter-force is equally aggressive. The movement now spans 8+ states (TX, TN, WI, VA, NY, CO, AR, CA, IN). Governor Abbott's June 10 directive to PUC/ERCOT requiring DCs to fund their own grid infrastructure adds a new regulatory tier between county action and federal legislation.
**Watch next week:** Abbott PUC/ERCOT joint memo due July 17; Hochul's signing decision; Shawano County WI vote June 24.

**3. NVIDIA Extends Vertical Infrastructure Play**
NVIDIA signed a $5.5B deal with IREN ($2.1B equity option + $3.4B managed GPU cloud services) covering a 5 GW pipeline anchored by a 2 GW flagship in Sweetwater TX built to NVIDIA's DSX architecture spec. This follows the $40B equity stack announced at Computex and the Vera Rubin full-production announcement. NVIDIA is now buying into the physical layer — power, land, buildings — not just selling chips.
**Watch next week:** Whether other GPU cloud operators seek similar equity-backed partnerships.

**4. Gas Plant Cost Spiral Strengthens Alternatives**
BNEF data showed gas plant construction costs up 66% since 2023 ($2,157/kW), turbine prices 195% above 2019, and build timelines 23% longer. GE Vernova's 100 GW backlog (targeting 110 GW by year-end) and Siemens Energy's €136B record backlog confirm slots are sold into the next decade. Google's 100 MW VPP deal with Voltus in PJM — the first hyperscaler-VPP wholesale market transaction — looks less like an experiment and more like a rational response to gas economics.
**Watch next week:** Whether other hyperscalers announce VPP or demand-response deals in PJM or ERCOT.

---

## Predictions Update

- **#2 (rural moratoriums):** Already confirmed — additional counties keep piling on. The prediction understated the pace.
- **#5 (Hill County TX rescission):** Confirmed June 5 via $100M lawsuit.
- **#11 (Hochul signs NY moratorium):** Strengthening — strong legislative margins, no public opposition from Governor's office.
- **#12 (more TX county rescissions via lawsuits):** Strengthening — Hood County approved a DC project under lawsuit threat this week.
- **#13 (Abbott directive produces enforceable TX rules):** On track — joint memo due July 17.
- **#14 (more hyperscaler-VPP deals):** Strengthening — Google-Voltus sets the template.
- **#15 (Anthropic export ban reversed/narrowed):** New this week, pending.

No predictions busted.

---

## Cross-Sector Patterns

- **Regulatory fragmentation accelerating.** County moratoriums, governor directives, state legislation, federal bills, and FERC rulemaking are all advancing simultaneously with no coordination. The result is a patchwork where developers face different rules county-by-county, state-by-state. Expect forum-shopping to intensify — developers will target jurisdictions with the fewest restrictions, which currently means unincorporated rural areas in states without home-rule authority.

- **Gas bottleneck + cost inflation creating structural demand for alternative capacity.** The Google-Voltus VPP, NuScale/TVA SMR pipeline, and Constellation Crane nuclear restart are no longer hedges. With gas plant costs at $2,157/kW and rising, they're becoming the rational path for hyperscalers who need power in 2–3 years, not a decade.

- **Export controls as infrastructure geography driver.** If the Anthropic Fable/Mythos ban holds, compliance-driven domestic-only deployments could accelerate rural data center siting in the U.S. — converging with the moratorium counter-force in an unpredictable way.

## Next Week Watch

- **FERC RM26-4 large-load interconnection rule** — due by end of June; could drop any day. The 20 MW threshold and cost-allocation framework will shape every data center interconnection for the next decade.
- **OpenAI GPT-5.6 release** — Polymarket 83% odds for June 22–28 window. Competitive positioning against Anthropic (hobbled by export ban) matters.
- **Shawano County WI moratorium vote** — June 24. If passed, Wisconsin will have two county moratoriums and growing pressure for state-level action.

**Note:** Only one daily briefing ran this week (June 17). This digest covers the full arc from June 1–17 to capture how narratives evolved across the briefing series.

## Top Movers

### 1. Data center moratorium movement goes national
The single most persistent story across all six briefings. It started with Hill County TX (June 1), spread to Tennessee and Wisconsin (June 3–4), and by June 17 reached the state level: New York's legislature passed the Responsible Data Center Development Act (Senate 44-16, Assembly 102-39), the first state moratorium bill. Denver enacted a unanimous one-year pause. Superior WI followed. Meanwhile, Hill County TX rescinded its moratorium June 5 after RCM Hill LLC's $100M federal lawsuit — establishing developer litigation as a counter-force. The movement now spans 7+ states (TX, TN, WI, VA, NY, CO, AR). **Watch next week:** Governor Hochul's response to the NY bill; Shawano County WI board vote June 24.

### 2. SpaceX IPO opens the AI-adjacent listing window
SpaceX priced at $135/share June 11, raised ~$75B (largest U.S. IPO ever), and closed +19% on day one under ticker SPCX. This gives Anthropic (S-1 under SEC review, $965B valuation) and OpenAI (filing expected) a live pricing benchmark. Combined 2026 listings could pull $200B+ from public markets. **Watch:** Anthropic pricing timeline (target: October) and whether secondary-market multiples compress after the initial euphoria.

### 3. Gas turbine bottleneck hardens into a structural constraint
GE Vernova's backlog hit 100 GW in Q1 (targeting 110 GW by year-end), with Q1 orders +71% YoY to $18.3B. Siemens Energy reported €136B record backlog and committed $1B to U.S. manufacturing. All three OEMs (GE, Siemens, MHI) are sold out into the next decade. This appeared in every briefing from June 1 onward and directly explains the SMR deal pipeline (NuScale/TVA 6 GW, Oklo 14 GW, Constellation Crane restart). **Watch:** Whether GE Vernova hits 110 GW by Q4; whether turbine lead times (now 5–7 years) force utilities to accelerate nuclear.

### 4. FERC large-load rule (RM26-4-000) still pending
First flagged June 1 as "due by end of June." Still pending as of June 17. Key debates: 20 MW threshold, 60-day expedited studies, cost allocation. SPP's HILL initiative serves as interim model. Simultaneously, the Power for the People Act (Warner/Van Hollen) attacks the demand side by requiring DCs to bring their own generation. **Watch:** Rule release before July 1.

### 5. PJM capacity costs expose rate pressure
The $16.4B auction (June 2) showed DCs driving 40% of costs. By June 17, three-auction cumulative hit $47.2B, with 2027/28 adding 5,250 MW peak load (5,100 MW = data centers). Ratepayers face +$1.4B in capacity costs starting June 2026. This is the economic fuel behind the moratorium movement.
